subject: Proposal: fee exposure model & annual silo for liability cap
messages:
From: Kevin O'Rourke <kevin@brightline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightline.com>, Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA redline – liability cap construct

Sergio — attaching our redline of the MSA. Two quick asks from legal/procurement: 1) move the liability cap to an aggregate fixed-cap (not resetting annually) equal to 2x total fees; 2) narrow carve-outs for consequential damages but preserve IP infringement and gross negligence carveouts.

We think an aggregate cap is standard for our auditors and finance. Please let me know if Redwood can accept aggregate exposure or if you need to propose an alternative that keeps us compliant.

Attachments: Brightline_MSA_Redline_20260914.docx (docx, 132KB)

Thanks —
Kevin O'Rourke
Head of Procurement, Brightline Health
kevin@brightline.com
(415) 555-0198

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Rourke <kevin@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline – liability cap construct

Kevin — thanks for the redline and the note. I looped in Kimberly and Karthik from legal/pricing. Broadly, Redwood's standard position is: aggregate cap equal to the greater of $500k or 1x fees paid in the prior 12-month period, with certain carve-outs (IP indemnity, gross negligence, willful misconduct). We prefer an annual reset because a per-year basis aligns with how customers consume and keeps economics predictable for both sides.

Can you confirm whether Brightline's auditors will only accept an aggregate (single pot) cap, or whether they would accept a per-year reset that we commit to in the Order Form? If aggregate is non-negotiable we can propose an alternate compromise (see below) — but need clarity from your side.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 14:28:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: draft compromise language for Brightline (liability schedule)

Team — draft compromise language below for Sergio to share. High level: offer an Order Form option that selects either (A) aggregate cap = greater of $750k or 1.5x fees paid in first 12 months, or (B) annual reset cap = greater of $400k or 1.0x fees per 12-month billing period. Both include standard carve-outs (IP indemnity, gross negligence, fraud, violations of law). Also propose a data-breach carveout cap of $5M limited to specific breach liabilities agreed in a separate schedule.

Pros/cons:
- Aggregate (A) protects customer finance but increases Redwood exposure; use only when customer insists and for larger enterprise deals.
- Annual (B) keeps Redwood unit economics predictable and maps to billing cadence; preferred.

If we share this, we should make clear the Order Form must explicitly select (A) or (B).

Kimberly
Sr. Counsel, Contracts

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Rourke <kevin@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline – liability cap construct

Kevin — appreciate the quick review. Brightline's aggregate ask is understood. To keep this moving, Redwood can offer two negotiated options that the Order Form can pick:

Option 1 (Enterprise aggregate): aggregate cap equal to the greater of $750,000 or 1.5x Total Fees paid under the Order Form (all periods combined). This option includes carve-outs for IP indemnity, gross negligence, willful misconduct, and payment obligations.

Option 2 (Annual reset – preferred): per-12-month cap equal to the greater of $400,000 or 1.0x Fees invoiced in the prior 12 months; cap resets each 12-month period. Carve-outs as above; for data breach we propose a separate capped exposure schedule (we've attached a one-page liability schedule).

If procurement needs aggregate for auditing, Option 1 should be acceptable; Option 2 is our standard for self-serve / PLG customers and aligns better with unit economics. Please confirm which option Brightline will select in the Order Form. If they must have aggregate but at a lower multiplier, propose a target and we'll review.

Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_Liability_Schedule_20260916.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

Thanks —
Sergio

From: Kevin O'Rourke <kevin@brightline.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Legal <legal@brightline.com>, Brightline Procurement <procurement@brightline.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2026 11:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA redline – liability cap construct

Sergio — appreciate the two options. Procurement prefers Option 1 (aggregate) for audit simplicity. Legal has one ask: reduce Redwood's aggregate multiplier to 1.25x fees (from 1.5x). They will keep the IP/ gross negligence carve-outs.

Can Redwood accept aggregate = greater of $650,000 or 1.25x Total Fees? If not, we need to understand the bottom-line number Redwood can agree to so we can route the internal approval.

Kevin

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin O'Rourke <kevin@brightline.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA redline – liability cap construct

Kevin — thanks. Quick internal check with finance/legal: Redwood can accept aggregate = greater of $700,000 or 1.35x Total Fees, limited to liabilities arising during the initial 24-month term (with a one-time post-term run-off for active claims notified in term). Carve-outs remain as discussed. That gives both sides a predictable ceiling while moving closer to Brightline's requested multiplier.

If Brightline is comfortable with 1.35x (floor $700k) and a 24-month term limit, we'll draft final order-form language for signature. If procurement counters, escalate to contract execs and we can set up a 30-minute call Monday to finalize.

Best,
Sergio
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
